garcia_ruiz_2016.kunye: García-Ruiz A., Cole J.B., VanRaden P.M., Wiggans G.R., Ruiz-López F.J., Van Tassell C.P. 2016. Changes in genetic selection differentials and generation intervals in US Holstein dairy cattle as a result of genomic selection. PNAS 113(28).
alinti: Seven years after the introduction of genomic selection in the United States, it is now possible to evaluate the impact of this technology on the population.
The SB GI reduced from ∼7 y to less than 2.5 y, and the DB GI fell from about 4 y to nearly 2.5 y.
The most dramatic response to genomic selection was observed for the lowly heritable traits DPR, PL, and SCS.
resulting in rapid genetic improvement in fertility, lifespan, and health in a breed where these traits eroded over time.
rates of genetic gain per year increased from ∼50-100% for yield traits and from threefold to fourfold for lowly heritable traits.

morgounov_2019_iwwip.kunye: Morgounov A., Özdemir F., Keser M., Akın B., Payne T., Braun H.-J. 2019. International Winter Wheat Improvement Program: history, activities, impact and future. Frontiers of Agricultural Science and Engineering 6(3).
morgounov_2019_iwwip._tarih: Değerlendirme 2019'da yayımlandı; rakamlar o tarihin durumu. Metin tarihini yazar.
alinti: International Winter Wheat Improvement Program (IWWIP) was established in 1986 between the Government of Turkey and CIMMYT
ICARDA joined the program in 1991 making it a three-way partnership
distributed to more than 100 cooperators in all continents
A total of 93 IWWIP cultivars have been released in 11 countries occupying annually an estimated 2.5–3.0 Mha.
This established winter wheat breeding system takes 9–10 years from the cross to international distribution.
An alternative faster system was started in 2018 using a speed breeding facility in Izmir allowing two to three generations per year.
Until recently, the IWWIP remained largely a conventional breeding program.
In 2017, IWWIP breeders analyzed functional and random KASP markers on a large germplasm set (exceeding 1500)
In 2018, all FAWWON candidates were genotyped for functional KASP markers.
Normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) measurements taken with a hand-held crop sensor, have been routinely used for germplasm evaluation especially at a preliminary yield testing stage.
IWWIP organized phenotyping workshop in 2018 in Konya laying a foundation for wider application of modern phenotyping tools.
IWWIP initiated and conducted a national inventory of wheat landraces in Turkey in 2009–2014
More than 60 of the 81 provinces in Turkey were visited by survey and collection teams, and wheat landraces were identified and collected from more than 1500 farms.

The future strategy will be based on combining an effective conventional approach with application of new modern tools including precision and high throughput phenotyping, application of genomic tools and molecular markers, speed breeding to accelerate the genetic gains.

michel_2016.kunye: Michel S., Ametz C., Gungor H., Akgöl B., Epure D., Grausgruber H., Löschenberger F., Buerstmayr H. 2016. Genomic assisted selection for enhancing line breeding: merging genomic and phenotypic selection in winter wheat breeding programs with preliminary yield trials. Theoretical and Applied Genetics 130(2).
alinti: Early generation genomic selection is superior to conventional phenotypic selection in line breeding
The selection of lines that enter resource-demanding multi-environment trials is a crucial decision in every line breeding program
The prediction accuracy using only phenotypic data was rather low (r = 0.21) for grain yield
Genomic selection models were nevertheless found to be superior to conventional phenotypic selection for predicting grain yield performance of lines across years (r = 0.39).
This genomic assisted selection led to a 20% increase in prediction accuracy

watson_2018.kunye: Watson A., Ghosh S., Williams M.J. ve ark. 2018. Speed breeding is a powerful tool to accelerate crop research and breeding. Nature Plants 4(1).
alinti: This slow improvement rate is attributed partly to the long generation times of crop plants.

Speed breeding can be used to achieve up to 6 generations per year for spring wheat (Triticum aestivum), durum wheat (T. durum), barley (Hordeum vulgare), chickpea (Cicer arietinum) and pea (Pisum sativum), and 4 generations for canola (Brassica napus), instead of 2-3 under normal glasshouse conditions.
We envisage great potential for integrating speed breeding with other modern crop breeding technologies, including high-throughput genotyping, genome editing and genomic selection
We demonstrate that speed breeding in fully enclosed, controlled-environment growth chambers can accelerate plant development
The use of supplemental lighting in a glasshouse environment allows rapid generation cycling

montesinos_lopez_2021.kunye: Montesinos-López O.A., Montesinos-López A., Pérez-Rodríguez P., Barrón-López J.A., Martini J.W.R., Fajardo-Flores S.B., Gaytan-Lugo L.S., Santana-Mancilla P.C., Crossa J. 2021. A review of deep learning applications for genomic selection. BMC Genomics 22.
montesinos_lopez_2021.tur: derleme — derin öğrenme ile genomik seçilim
alinti: In recent years, deep learning (DL) methods have been considered in the context of genomic prediction.
The main requirement for using DL is the quality and sufficiently large training data.
we did not find clear superiority of DL in terms of prediction power compared to conventional genome based prediction models.
Nevertheless, there are clear evidences that DL algorithms capture nonlinear patterns more efficiently than conventional genome based.
Deep learning algorithms are able to integrate data from different sources as is usually needed in GS assisted breeding
It is important to apply DL to large training-testing data sets.

alinti: Insights into Drought Tolerance of Tetraploid Wheat Genotypes in the Germination Stage Using Machine Learning Algorithms
Department of Field Crops, Faculty of Agriculture, Ankara University
Poznań University of Life Sciences
this study sought to evaluate the responses of distinct wheat genotypes to diverse levels of drought stress encountered during the germination stage

The induction of drought stress was achieved using polyethylene glycol at varying concentrations, and the assessment was conducted through the application of multivariate analysis and machine learning algorithms.
Predictions were then generated using four distinct machine learning techniques.
offering a fast and cost-effective approach
